The Solvay Conference on Electrons and Photons, Brussels. 1927. 17 of the 29 attendees were or became Nobel Prize winners.

The Solvay Conference, founded by the Belgian industrialist Ernest Solvay in 1912, was considered a turning point in the world of physics. This particular year, the world’s most notable physicists met to discuss the newly formulated quantum theory. The leading figures were Albert Einstein and Niels Bohr. Note that Marie Curie was the lone female in attendance.
